summary: Defines an experimental extension to IKEv2 that lets an IKE Security Association be created and authenticated using the EAP Re-authentication Protocol described in RFC 6696. It updates RFC 5996.

eli5.summary: If you already showed your ID once, this lets you get back into a secure room quickly with a shortcut, instead of showing it all over again.

questions: how to use eap re-authentication with ikev2
how does erp speed up vpn re-authentication
subtitle: A fast way to re-authenticate VPN connections using EAP without repeating the full authentication.

tldr.problem: IKEv2 can authenticate users with EAP, but EAP authentication is slow and requires many round trips and user interaction. Users who need multiple VPN tunnels must authenticate each time, which is cumbersome.
tldr.mechanism: This extension lets IKEv2 use ERP (EAP Re-authentication Protocol), which allows a user to prove they already authenticated somewhere else without repeating the full EAP process. It reuses the re-authentication key (rMSK) stored on both the VPN client and the server.
tldr.outcome: Subsequent tunnel connections are much faster and require no user interaction, making it practical for users to create multiple VPN tunnels to different gateways in the same domain or to reconnect after disconnection.

today: RFC 6867 is Experimental and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 5996 (IKEv2) to support ERP-based authentication. This specification remains available for implementation but requires backend AAA servers to support RFC 6696.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 6867 extends IKEv2 (Internet Key Exchange version 2) to support ERP, the EAP Re-authentication Protocol defined in RFC 6696. IKEv2 can already authenticate users with EAP (Extensible Authentication Protocol), but this creates two problems: the authentication process requires many round trips and may require user interaction each time, making it slow and inconvenient for creating multiple IPsec tunnels or reconnecting after a disconnection.

The RFC brings together two existing technologies. ERP allows a user to authenticate once and then quickly re-authenticate to other systems without repeating the full EAP process. By combining this with IKEv2, remote access clients can now create multiple VPN tunnels or reconnect after network outages, device suspension, or temporary moves out of range, all without user intervention. The extension uses a re-authentication Master Session Key (rMSK) shared between the client and server, similar to session resumption mechanisms.
sections.eli5: Imagine showing your ID card once to the security desk. After that, every time you come back, you just flash a temporary pass instead of showing your full ID again. That's what this RFC does for VPN connections.

sections.title: How ERP Works in IKEv2
sections.content:
The protocol uses a modified IKE exchange. In the initial SA setup (IKE_SA_INIT), the responder (VPN gateway) signals support for ERP with a special Notify message containing the domain name. If the initiator (VPN client) has an unexpired re-authentication key for that domain from a previous authentication, it sends an EAP-Initiate/Re-auth message in the first IKE_AUTH request instead of starting a full EAP exchange.

The responder forwards this message to the backend AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) server. If the server has a valid re-authentication key for that session, it responds with an EAP-Finish/Re-auth message and the rMSK. The responder forwards this back to the initiator. Both sides then use this rMSK as the session key to calculate the AUTH payloads that complete the IKE_AUTH exchange. If the AAA server does not have a valid key, it responds with a regular EAP request, and the full EAP authentication flow proceeds as normal.
sections.eli5: The gateway says 'Do you already have a re-auth pass?' The client sends the pass. The server checks the pass, and if it's valid, says 'OK, come in.' No password needed.

sections.title: Identity and Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC does not send the user's real identity during re-authentication. Instead, the initiator sends an ephemeral ID derived from the Extended Master Session Key (EMSKName), encoded as part of a Network Access Identifier (NAI). The responder only learns the domain name from the Notify message, not the user's actual identity.

This design allows the VPN gateway to make policy decisions based on the domain name alone, if sufficient for authorization. If user-specific information is needed, the gateway must obtain it from the AAA server through attribute extensions such as the CLASS attribute in RADIUS, or by querying the server separately using protocols like LDAP. The RFC emphasizes that if the server supporting re-authentication is different from the one that did the original authentication, careful coordination of user information is required, and a compliant implementation MAY reject initiators for which it cannot make authorization decisions.
sections.eli5: The security desk sees you have a valid re-auth pass and which company you're from, but they don't know your name. If they need to know your name to let you in, they have to check with the main office.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC notes that the specification does not mandate how re-authentication keys are stored or how long they are valid; these operational issues are covered in RFC 6696. The responder MAY alert the user and log the event if the client has a valid re-authentication key but the server does not, which could indicate either loss of state on the server or a potential security concern.

If the server does not have a valid key when the client sends the re-authentication request, the server responds with a regular EAP request, and the IKEv2 initiator and EAP client proceed with full EAP authentication as if ERP were not being used. This ensures backward compatibility with systems that do not support ERP. For full re-authentication, the backend AAA server must support RFC 6696, but the IKEv2 peers themselves require only this extension.
sections.eli5: If the re-auth pass is lost or expired on either side, the system automatically falls back to the normal full authentication, so nothing breaks.
